bioanalytical_method: INDIRECT: plasma concentration was estimated from an ex vivo anti-HIV-1 inhibition assay, taking the highest dilution causing 50% inhibition, rather than by a chemical assay
bioanalytical_quote: The highest dilution-fold of the plasma sample causing 50% inhibition of HIV-1 infection was calculated, based on which the concentration of an active peptide in plasma was estimated
notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the PK parameter table: PEG2kC34 2.57 ± 0.71 h and PEG5kC34 5.11 ± 3.54 h, both subcutaneous at 1.7 μmol/kg, n = 4 (2 male, 2 female). THE ASSAY IS A BIOACTIVITY PROXY, NOT A CONCENTRATION MEASUREMENT. Plasma levels were inferred from the dilution of plasma causing 50% inhibition of HIV-1 infection, so what decays with these half-lives is antiviral ACTIVITY; any inactive metabolite is invisible and any matrix effect on the assay reads as concentration. PEPlife2 records the assay as 'N.A.', losing that distinction. Note the SD on PEG5kC34 is 3.54 h on a 5.11 h mean, so the 2-fold separation between the two conjugates is not well resolved at n = 4. Finally, the two PEPlife2 sequences differ by a single leading cysteine (CWMEW... vs WMEW...), which is almost certainly the PEG attachment residue rather than a real design difference; as stored, the 2-fold half-life difference driven by 2 kDa vs 5 kDa of PEG is represented as the presence or absence of one Cys.
